calls.reason: Tesla's reported budget cut does not identify NVIDIA spending, and Meta's possible substitution accompanied broad-market gains. Neither establishes the claimed trigger and resulting market harm.

The Register documents serious Replit damage, but METR finds mixed capabilities and studies supervised productivity. These do not establish a general tendency for unchecked agents to cause breakage and extra work.

Apollo's index data and NVIDIA's filing establish concentration, but neither shows immediate losses for chip buyers or market dependence on their purchases. The historical fragility ranking remains unsupported.

Anthropic reports team redeployment and Klarna reports automated workloads, but neither independently establishes broad replacement of white-collar workers. Present employment findings cannot settle a prediction of permanent impossibility.

The Deep Dive reports substantial historical serving costs, while MacRumors documents paid Labs offerings. Neither supplies the full economics needed to establish or rule out a viable route to profit.
Amazon's filings show much smaller annual company-wide capex in 2012–2014 than in 2024, but do not establish cumulative early AWS spending. The inflation-adjusted comparison remains uncertain.
